pr_body:
When the user says they would like to reflect on a type/method and the type/method is generic and they don't provide the instantiation, we need to come up with some instantiation so that we can generate some code (with the hopes that the code will be shareable with whatever instantiation is actually needed at runtime).

E.g. if they want to reflect on `SomeMethod<T>`, we try to generate `SomeMethod<object>` that is actually backed by code that can be reused for any reference type T. (More on that here: https://twitter.com/MStrehovsky/status/1244602445461950470).

`GetTypeThatMeetsConstraints` is a heuristic that tries to come up with a usable instantiation if generic constraints are involved.

The heuristic needs to be enlightened about the fact that with static abstract methods, not all interfaces are usable (e.g. `SomeMethod<T> where T : IMyInterface` - if the interface has static abstract methods, `SomeMethod<IMyInterface>` is not a legal instantiation.

This fix is somewhat more aggressive because e.g. the below would be still okay:

```csharp
static void Blah<T> where T : IFoo { T.Blah() }
interface IFoo { static virtual void Blah() { /* default implementation */ }
```

We would ideally want to validate the constraints in full. TypeSystemConstraintsHelpers (used mostly for the non-shipping ILVerify project) wasn't updated for static abstracts though, so it doesn't help.

It's unclear how much value is there in this heuristic now that we pivoted to relying more on static analysis and compile-time warnings.

Anyway, we need to prevent the bad instantiation from entering the system.

Fixes #68538. Fixes #69223.

review_comments: Just curious for my education: canon can't be used in these cases because it can't fulfill certain constraints, right?

It will use __Canon (or even __UniversalCanon if universal shared code is available, which it isn't) if `allowCanon` is true, but we can't currently use __Canon everywhere:

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/5369b096c4675df82c923e5fd0d278465f8feb79/src/coreclr/tools/Common/Compiler/TypeExtensions.cs#L642

There's a file format limitation around generic methods (and the bug happens in a mal-instantiated generic method):

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/8e8a62156ea459945b1d953c4fbe950d276bbc9b/src/coreclr/tools/aot/ILCompiler.Compiler/Compiler/RootingHelpers.cs#L67-L70
